questions.question: What does NAT stand for?

explanation.correct: NAT stands for Network Address Translation — it replaces private IPs with a public IP for outbound internet communication.
explanation.why: The other options are invented terms. NAT is a standard networking concept used to allow private networks to communicate with the internet.

questions.question: Which type of subnet should a NAT Gateway be placed in?

explanation.correct: NAT Gateway must be placed in a public subnet because it needs a path to the Internet Gateway to forward traffic to the internet.
explanation.why: If placed in a private subnet, the NAT Gateway itself would have no internet access and couldn't forward traffic.

questions.question: What resource must be attached to a NAT Gateway when creating it?

explanation.correct: An Elastic IP (static public IP) must be assigned to the NAT Gateway — this becomes its public-facing IP address used for all outbound traffic.
explanation.why: Security Groups are not associated with NAT Gateway. The Internet Gateway and Route Table are separate components.

questions.question: What is the maximum bandwidth that NAT Gateway can auto-scale to?

explanation.correct: NAT Gateway automatically scales up to 45 Gbps of bandwidth — no manual resizing needed.
explanation.why: This is a key exam fact. NAT Instance, by contrast, is limited by the EC2 instance type you choose.

questions.question: What must be disabled on a NAT Instance to allow it to forward traffic?

explanation.correct: Source/Destination Check must be disabled on a NAT Instance. By default, EC2 drops packets where it is not the source or destination. NAT forwards packets for other instances, so this check must be turned off.
explanation.why: The other options are not related to NAT forwarding functionality.

questions.question: Which protocol does AWS Site-to-Site VPN use for encryption?

explanation.correct: AWS Site-to-Site VPN uses IPSec (Internet Protocol Security) for encrypting the tunnel between on-premises and AWS.
explanation.why: SSL/TLS is for web traffic, SSH is for remote access, HTTPS is the application layer. VPN tunneling uses IPSec at the network layer.

questions.question: What is the AWS-side endpoint of a Site-to-Site VPN connection called?

explanation.correct: The Virtual Private Gateway (VGW) is the AWS-side endpoint of a VPN connection. It is attached to your VPC and receives the VPN tunnel from your on-premises network.
explanation.why: Customer Gateway represents your on-premises router. Internet Gateway provides public internet access. NAT Gateway handles NAT.

questions.question: What represents the on-premises router in an AWS Site-to-Site VPN setup?

explanation.correct: The Customer Gateway (CGW) represents your on-premises router or firewall device in the AWS console. You create a CGW and enter your router's public IP address.
explanation.why: VGW is the AWS-side. Transit Gateway is for connecting multiple VPCs. VPN Endpoint is not the correct term.

questions.question: Is AWS Direct Connect encrypted by default?

options.text: Yes — it uses IPSec by default
No — it is not encrypted by default
Only if you pay for the encryption add-on

explanation.correct: Direct Connect is NOT encrypted by default. It is a private dedicated connection, but the data is not encrypted. You must add a VPN on top of Direct Connect if you need encryption.
explanation.why: This is the most common exam trap for Direct Connect. Privacy (no internet) ≠ Encryption.

questions.question: How long does it typically take to provision an AWS Direct Connect connection?

explanation.correct: Direct Connect typically takes weeks to provision because it involves physical infrastructure — ordering fiber, arranging colocation, and physically installing and testing the cable.
explanation.why: VPN can be set up in hours. Direct Connect requires physical work that takes weeks. This setup time difference is a key exam point.

questions.question: A company has private EC2 instances in 3 Availability Zones. How many NAT Gateways are needed for full high availability?

options.text: 6 — two per Availability Zone for redundancy

explanation.correct: NAT Gateway is highly available within a single AZ but not across AZs. For full HA, you need one NAT Gateway per AZ. If one AZ's NAT Gateway fails, other AZs continue working independently.
explanation.why: One per VPC would mean all AZs share one NAT Gateway — if it fails or its AZ has an outage, all private instances lose internet access.

questions.question: What is the approximate bandwidth limit per VPN tunnel in AWS Site-to-Site VPN?

explanation.correct: Each AWS Site-to-Site VPN tunnel supports approximately 1.25 Gbps of bandwidth. This is a key limitation compared to Direct Connect which supports 1 Gbps, 10 Gbps, or higher.
explanation.why: The 1.25 Gbps limit makes VPN unsuitable for massive data transfer workloads that require higher throughput.

questions.question: Which feature does NAT Instance support that NAT Gateway does NOT?

explanation.correct: NAT Instance supports custom iptables rules, giving you full control over routing and traffic filtering. NAT Gateway has limited custom routing options and does not support iptables.
explanation.why: NAT Gateway supports auto-scaling and HA. NAT Instance does not auto-scale. Both can use Elastic IPs.

questions.question: A NAT Gateway was created but private instances still can't access the internet. What is the MOST likely cause?

options.text: The NAT Gateway doesn't have an Elastic IP
The private subnet's route table doesn't have a route to the NAT Gateway
The NAT Gateway is in the wrong region
Security Groups are blocking the NAT Gateway

explanation.correct: The most common mistake is forgetting to update the private subnet's route table. You must add a route: 0.0.0.0/0 → NAT Gateway ID. Without this route, private instances don't know to send internet traffic through the NAT Gateway.
explanation.why: NAT Gateway requires an EIP at creation, so A is unlikely if it was created successfully. Security Groups are not directly applied to NAT Gateway.

questions.question: How many IPSec tunnels does a single AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection create?

explanation.correct: Each Site-to-Site VPN connection automatically creates two IPSec tunnels for redundancy. If one tunnel fails, traffic automatically moves to the second tunnel.
explanation.why: The two-tunnel redundancy is a built-in reliability feature of AWS VPN — you don't need to configure it separately.

questions.question: Which AWS service acts as a central hub to connect multiple VPCs and on-premises networks together?

explanation.correct: Transit Gateway is a network transit hub that allows multiple VPCs and on-premises networks to connect through a single central gateway, using a hub-and-spoke model.
explanation.why: VPC Peering connects only two VPCs and doesn't scale well. Internet Gateway is for public internet access. Direct Connect Gateway is a specific component within Direct Connect architecture.

questions.question: A startup needs to connect its 5-person office to an AWS VPC for development purposes. They need it set up today. What is the best option?

options.text: Site-to-Site VPN — fast setup, low cost
Public internet — no extra setup needed

explanation.correct: Site-to-Site VPN is the best choice here — it can be set up in hours, is low cost, and is suitable for small workloads like a 5-person dev team. Direct Connect takes weeks and is expensive.
explanation.why: Direct Connect is overkill for a small startup. Public internet without VPN exposes traffic. VPN provides the right balance of speed, security, and cost.

questions.question: Which Direct Connect Virtual Interface type is used to access resources inside a VPC?

explanation.correct: Private VIF is used to access resources inside a VPC. Public VIF is used to access AWS public services (S3, DynamoDB endpoints, etc.) over Direct Connect without going through the internet.
explanation.why: The naming makes sense: Private VIF → private VPC resources. Public VIF → publicly addressable AWS services.

questions.question: NAT Gateway pricing includes which two components?

options.text: Per-hour charge + per-GB data processing charge

explanation.correct: NAT Gateway charges you per hour that it's provisioned (even if no traffic flows) plus per GB of data processed. This is why deleting unused NAT Gateways saves money.
explanation.why: NAT Instance only charges for the EC2 instance cost — there's no per-GB processing fee, making it potentially cheaper for high-traffic but low-maintenance environments.

questions.question: An enterprise needs to connect its on-premises data center to AWS with guaranteed low latency for a financial trading application. The connection must be highly reliable. What is the BEST solution?

explanation.correct: Direct Connect provides consistent, guaranteed low latency through a dedicated private fiber connection — ideal for latency-sensitive financial trading applications requiring high reliability.
explanation.why: VPN over the internet has variable latency — unacceptable for trading applications. Multiple VPNs still use the internet and don't solve the latency problem.

questions.question: A company uses Direct Connect as its primary connection to AWS. The network team wants to ensure connectivity is maintained if the fiber is ever cut. What should they set up as a failover?

options.text: An Internet Gateway on the VPC
A NAT Gateway for failover routing

explanation.correct: The standard AWS best practice is to use a Site-to-Site VPN as backup for Direct Connect. If the fiber is cut or the Direct Connect location has an issue, BGP routing automatically fails over to the VPN tunnel, maintaining connectivity.
explanation.why: A second DX connection is expensive and the cut might affect both if they share physical infrastructure. IGW and NAT Gateway don't provide on-premises connectivity.

questions.question: A security audit requires that all data between on-premises and AWS be encrypted in transit. The company currently uses Direct Connect. What change is needed?

options.text: No change — Direct Connect is encrypted by default
Enable encryption in the Direct Connect console settings
Layer a Site-to-Site VPN tunnel on top of the Direct Connect connection
Switch to a public VIF instead of private VIF

explanation.correct: Direct Connect is not encrypted by default. To add encryption, you layer a Site-to-Site VPN tunnel on top of the Direct Connect connection. This combines the performance of DX with the encryption of IPSec VPN.
explanation.why: There is no built-in encryption toggle for Direct Connect. Switching to public VIF doesn't add encryption. The solution is DX + VPN together.

questions.question: You have 10 VPCs and need them all to communicate with each other and with your on-premises network. Without Transit Gateway, how many VPC peering connections would be needed?

explanation.correct: Full mesh peering for n VPCs requires n*(n-1)/2 connections. For 10 VPCs: 10*9/2 = 45 peering connections. This shows why Transit Gateway (which needs only 10 connections) is essential at scale.
explanation.why: This formula comes from combinatorics — every VPC needs to connect to every other VPC exactly once. As VPCs grow, the number of connections grows exponentially.

questions.question: A private EC2 instance in VPC subnet 10.0.2.0/24 needs to pull from the public npm registry. The subnet's route table has: 10.0.0.0/16 → local, 0.0.0.0/0 → igw-abc123. What is the problem?

options.text: The EC2 instance needs a public IP address
The route should point to a NAT Gateway, not the Internet Gateway
The CIDR block is wrong — should be /16
Nothing — this configuration is correct for a private subnet

explanation.correct: A private subnet's route table should point outbound traffic (0.0.0.0/0) to a NAT Gateway — not directly to the Internet Gateway. Routing private subnet traffic to IGW would either fail (no public IP on instance) or expose the instance to inbound internet traffic.
explanation.why: Internet Gateway is for public subnets where instances have public IPs. Private subnets use NAT Gateway to hide their private IPs and prevent inbound connections.

questions.question: Which combination provides the HIGHEST bandwidth AND encryption for an on-premises to AWS connection?

options.text: Direct Connect with Private VIF only
Direct Connect with a VPN tunnel on top

explanation.correct: Direct Connect provides 1–100 Gbps bandwidth with consistent low latency. Layering a VPN on top adds IPSec encryption. This combination gives you both high bandwidth AND encryption — the best of both worlds.
explanation.why: VPN alone is limited to ~1.25 Gbps. Direct Connect alone has no encryption. Two VPNs in parallel still only reach ~2.5 Gbps combined. DX + VPN is the enterprise best practice.

questions.question: What happens to traffic going from a private subnet instance to the internet when the NAT Gateway in the same AZ is deleted?

options.text: Traffic automatically routes to a NAT Gateway in another AZ
Traffic goes through the Internet Gateway instead
All outbound internet traffic from that subnet fails
AWS creates a new NAT Gateway automatically

explanation.correct: NAT Gateway does not automatically fail over across AZs. If the NAT Gateway is deleted or its AZ goes down, all private instances in that subnet lose outbound internet access. This is why you need one NAT Gateway per AZ.
explanation.why: There is no automatic cross-AZ failover for NAT Gateway. The route table still points to the deleted gateway, and traffic drops.

questions.question: A NAT Instance in a public subnet is not forwarding traffic for private instances. Source/Destination Check is already disabled. What else should you verify?

options.text: The NAT Instance's Security Group allows outbound traffic from the private subnet's CIDR
The NAT Instance is in the private subnet
The NAT Instance has an IPv6 address
NAT Instances don't use Security Groups

explanation.correct: Unlike NAT Gateway, a NAT Instance is a real EC2 instance with Security Groups. The Security Group on the NAT Instance must allow inbound traffic from the private subnet's CIDR range and outbound traffic to the internet.
explanation.why: This is a key difference from NAT Gateway — NAT Gateway doesn't use Security Groups, but NAT Instance does. Forgetting to configure Security Groups is a common NAT Instance setup mistake.

questions.question: A company architect says: 'We need a dedicated, consistent, low-latency link to AWS but we also need the data encrypted.' What is the correct architecture recommendation?

options.text: Direct Connect + Site-to-Site VPN tunnel on top

explanation.correct: Direct Connect + VPN combines the low latency and dedicated bandwidth of Direct Connect with the IPSec encryption of VPN. This is the recommended architecture when both performance and encryption are required.
explanation.why: DX alone has no encryption. VPN alone has variable latency. DX + VPN = consistent latency + encryption.

questions.question: Your company just acquired another company that runs its own AWS account with VPCs. You need to enable communication between your VPCs and their VPCs privately, at scale, across accounts. What is the BEST solution?

options.text: VPC Peering between every pair of VPCs
Transit Gateway with Resource Access Manager sharing
Direct Connect from both companies to the same location

explanation.correct: Transit Gateway can be shared across AWS accounts using AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM). This allows VPCs from both companies to connect through a single hub without managing hundreds of peering connections.
explanation.why: Full mesh VPC peering at scale is unmanageable. VPN is for on-premises connectivity. Direct Connect doesn't solve VPC-to-VPC routing.

questions.question: A solutions architect needs to choose between NAT Gateway and NAT Instance for a startup's development environment. Traffic is low (under 1 GB/day), budget is very tight, and the team needs SSH access to the NAT host for debugging. Which should they choose and why?

options.text: NAT Gateway — always the correct choice
NAT Instance — lower cost for low traffic AND supports SSH for debugging

explanation.correct: NAT Instance makes sense here for three reasons: (1) very low traffic means NAT Gateway's per-GB charges add up poorly; (2) NAT Instance supports SSH, allowing the team to use it as a bastion/jump host for debugging; (3) the startup budget constraint makes EC2-only pricing attractive. In production, NAT Gateway would be recommended.
explanation.why: NAT Gateway is the default for production, but NAT Instance has legitimate use cases. Internet Gateway can't replace NAT for private subnets. Direct Connect is for on-premises connectivity.
